title: In Conversation: Founder James on Phrasal Verbs, Tea, and the Quiet Season of Learning
dek: December is the slowest month of the magazine’s year, on purpose. Founder James (JY DM) on why phrasal verbs are logical rather than chaotic, what winter rituals teach us about retention, and how to end a year of study without grading yourself.

blocks.text: December closes the magazine’s year, and it is deliberately the quietest issue we publish. The theme is winter solstice warmth: seasonal rhythm, tea rituals, introspective living, and the very specific logic of phrasal verbs. It is a volume designed to be read slowly, in short sittings, beside a window. We asked the founder why a language magazine would choose stillness as its December theme.
blocks.say: December closes the magazine’s year, and it is deliberately the quietest issue we publish. The theme is winter solstice warmth: seasonal rhythm, tea rituals, introspective living, and the very specific logic of phrasal verbs.

blocks.text: This Month: Winter Grammar & High Frequency Verbs
blocks.say: This Month: Winter Grammar & High Frequency Verbs

blocks.text: Vol. 2026.12 pairs two things that look unrelated. The Grammar Made Cosy piece decodes phrasal verbs — how to read them, predict them, and invent new ones — while the Words desk publishes part two of the ten essential verbs series across fourteen languages. Around them, the issue keeps returning to seasonal ritual: warmth, repetition, and the small daily practices that make a language stick.
The argument is that winter is not a pause in learning. It is the season when consolidation happens.
